mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past 3 months indicates a shift toward monetary easing, which lowers the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% within the past month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which often precedes economic slowdowns and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is at or below 0.5% and the unemployment rate is at or below 5.0%, the combination of monetary easing and a strong labor market signals robust economic conditions, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary easing with strong labor market
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS <= 0.5% and UNRATE <= 5.0%, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle economic regime defined by high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) and slowing GDP growth (GDPC1 quarterly growth < 1.0%), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated monetary tightening and economic deceleration.
regime_hint: late-cycle expansion with high inflation and slowing GDP growth
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and GDPC1 quarterly growth < 1.0%, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 (index base 2017=100) signals a contraction in manufacturing and services, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO < 100.0, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A strong month-over-month increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 100 thousand jobs signals robust labor market conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investor confidence rises.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 100, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising housing starts (HOUST) above 1120.0 thousand units and strong industrial production (INDPRO) above 105.0 (index base 2017=100) signals robust consumer and business activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as economic expansion continues.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST > 1120.0 and INDPRO > 105.0, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in year-over-year consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL yoy > 3.0%) signals persistent inflation, which often leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the Federal Reserve is likely to raise rates.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL yoy > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.05.
